newsitem.title: USA: Kinkel expects strong G7 statement on Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel expects strong G7 statement on Bosnia.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Friday the Group of Seven summit should warn Bosnia clearly that it could only expect outside help if its feuding parts implemented the 1995 Dayton accords.

Kinkel said Bosnia would be a central point in the summit's political declaration and Russia, taking part in most meetings at the three-day gathering, should put pressure on the Bosnian Serbs to bring about progress on the ground.

In the latest sign of squabbling within Bosnia's inter- ethnic government, a fund-raising conference for the battered republic was postponed because Bosnia had failed to introduce needed economic reforms in time.
Kinkel said other aspects of the peace accord reached in Dayton, Ohio, such as the return of refugees and cooperation with war crimes enquiries, were also behind schedule.
"The civil implementation of the Dayton accord is going too slowly," he told reporters. "I hope we have a strong, a really strong declaration (on Bosnia).
"We should put more conditions on our aid. It must be clear that the world community is no longer ready to provide troops and pour in millions in aid if we don't move forward."
Stressing that Russia had played a constructive role in the five-nation contact group on Bosnia, Kinkel said: "I expect that Russia will put more pressure on the Bosnian Serb republic."
Kinkel said Croatian areas of Bosnia had shown most progress in implementing the Dayton accords, followed by Muslim areas and, far behind, the Serbian region.
"Money only goes, and should only go in the future, to where there is an echo," he said, referring to local support for implementing the Dayton accords.

The G7, which is expected to issue its statement on Bosnia on Sunday, comprises the United States, Japan, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Canada. Because Russia is taking part in nearly all sessions, the gathering has been dubbed "The Summit of the Eight".

The United States, hosting the Denver talks, has made clear it will call for a serious effort to build up democratic and social structures in Bosnia before the planned pull-out of its peacekeepiung troops from the country in July 1998.
